en: Thus have I heard: the Bākula Sutta, the 124th discourse of the Majjhima Nikāya.
On one occasion the Venerable Bākula was dwelling at Rājagaha in the Bamboo Grove, the Squirrels’ Feeding Place.
Then Acelaka Kassapa, a former householder friend of the Venerable Bākula, approached the Venerable Bākula and exchanged greetings with him.
When they had concluded their greetings and cordial conversation, he sat down to one side. Sitting there, Acelaka Kassapa said this to the Venerable Bākula:
“How long has it been since you went forth, friend Bākula?
“Friend, eighty years have passed since I went forth.
“But in these eighty years, friend Bākula, how many times have you engaged in sexual intercourse?”
“Friend Kassapa, you should not have asked me this:
‘But friend Bākula, how many times did you engage in sexual intercourse during these eighty years?
Rather, friend Kassapa, you should have asked me this:”
“But, friend Bākula, how many times have thoughts of sensual desire arisen in you during these eighty years?
“Friend, in the eighty years since I went forth, I do not recall a thought of sensual desire ever having arisen.
“That it has not occurred to the venerable Bākula in eighty years that a thought of sensual desire had ever arisen—this too we remember as a marvelous and wonderful quality of the venerable Bākula.”
“Friends, for eighty years since I went forth, I do not recall ever having experienced a perception of ill will...
nor a perception of cruelty.

“That the Venerable Bākula does not recall ever having experienced a perception of cruelty during eighty years—this too we shall remember as a marvelous and wonderful quality of the Venerable Bākula.”
“Friends, for eighty years since I went forth, I do not recall ever having had a thought of sensual desire arise.
“That the Venerable Bākula does not recall ever having had a thought of sensual desire arise in eighty years—this too we shall remember as a marvelous and wonderful quality of the Venerable Bākula.
“Friends, for eighty years since I went forth, I do not recall ever having had a thought of ill will arise... [and so on].
“...or thoughts of cruelty that had previously arisen.
“That the venerable Bākula does not recall having ever experienced thoughts of cruelty for eighty years—this too we remember as a marvelous and extraordinary quality of the venerable Bākula.
“Friends, for eighty years since my going forth, I do not recall ever having accepted a robe from a householder.”
“That the Venerable Bākula does not recall having accepted a householder’s robe in eighty years—this too we remember as a marvelous and wonderful quality of the Venerable Bākula.
“Friends, in the eighty years since I went forth, I do not recall ever having cut a robe with a blade.
“That the Venerable Bākula does not recall having cut a robe with a blade in eighty years... [as above] ...we remember.”
“Friends, for eighty years since I went forth, I do not recall ever having sewn a robe with a needle...
I do not recall ever having dyed a robe with dye...
I do not recall ever having sewn a robe during the kaṭhina period.”
I do not recall ever having deliberated with my fellow celibate practitioners regarding the work of robes...
I do not recall ever having accepted an invitation...
I do not recall ever having had such a thought arise before:
‘Oh, that someone would invite me!
… I do not recall ever sitting down inside a house [for a meal] … I do not recall ever eating inside a house …
I do not recall ever having taken a sign from the secondary characteristics of a woman...
I do not recall ever having taught the Dhamma to a woman, even so much as a four-line verse...
I do not recall ever having approached the dwelling place of bhikkhunīs...
I do not recall having taught the Dhamma to a bhikkhunī...
I do not recall having taught the Dhamma to a sikkhamānā...
I do not recall having taught the Dhamma to a sāmaṇerī...
I do not recall being one who gave the going-forth...
I do not recall being one who gave full ordination...
I do not recall being one who gave formal dependence...
I do not recall ever having had a novice attendant upon me...
I do not recall ever having bathed in a sauna...
I do not recall ever having bathed with scented powder.
I do not recall ever having had my limbs massaged by a fellow practitioner of the holy life...
I do not recall ever having suffered from an illness, even one as slight as a pinprick...
I do not recall ever having brought medicine, even so much as a piece of myrobalan fruit.
“I do not recall ever having used a bolster for support… I do not recall ever having made a bed.
“Since the Venerable One [has spoken thus]… we shall remember it.”
“Friends, for eighty years since I went forth, I do not recall ever having entered the rains retreat in a lodging within a village.
“That the Venerable Bākula does not recall entering the rains retreat in a lodging within a village for eighty years—this too we remember as a marvelous and wonderful quality of the Venerable Bākula.
“Friends, for only seven days did I eat almsfood in the kingdom while still under the protection [of my parents].”
Then, on the eighth day, full knowledge arose.

"That the venerable Bākula ate alms-food from the kingdom for only seven days, and then on the eighth day full knowledge arose—this too we remember as a marvelous and wonderful quality of the venerable Bākula.
Friend Bākula, may I receive the going-forth in this Dhamma and Vinaya; may I receive the full ordination."
Acelaka Kassapa received the going-forth in this Dhamma and Vinaya; he received full ordination.

Not long after his full ordination, dwelling alone, withdrawn, diligent, ardent, and resolute, the Venerable Kassapa—in no long time—attained that supreme goal of the holy life for the sake of which clansmen rightly go forth from the home life into homelessness.
Having realized it for himself through direct higher knowledge in this very life, he entered and dwelt therein.
He directly knew: "Birth is exhausted, the holy life has been lived, what was to be done has been done, there is no further state of being.
And so, the Venerable Kassapa became one of the Arahants.
Then, on a later occasion, the Venerable Bākula took his key and, approaching one monastery after another, spoke thus:
"Come forward, venerable sirs! Come forward, venerable sirs! Today my final Nibbāna will take place. [The monks asked:
"As for the fact that the Venerable Bākula, taking his key, approached one monastery after another and spoke thus: 'Come forward, venerable sirs...'"
"Come forward, venerable friends; today my final nibbāna will take place"—this too we remember as a marvelous and wonderful quality of the venerable Bākula.
While seated right there in the midst of the Saṅgha of bhikkhus, the venerable Bākula attained final nibbāna.
“That the Venerable Bākula attained final nibbāna while sitting right in the midst of the Saṅgha of bhikkhus—this too we remember as a marvelous and wonderful quality of the Venerable Bākula.
The Bākula Sutta, the fourth, is finished.
